check: why Home's scroll cost rose pass over pass (MS1)
how: Release walk build (MARQUEE_WALK_BUILD="DEBUG MARQUEE_WALK", own core from build-core.sh in the lane's checkout, arm64, app.momotus.walk) of trunk 24a953268 and of three candidates, with test(apple): the scroll walk says where it ran and what each pass left (views on the page after each pass, the pointer inside the window or not, the window shown or not); open -g -n, -MQMute YES, own -MQDataDir with MS1's addons, art cached on disk; each run started on a quiet Mac (one-minute load average under 4, at least 75 percent CPU idle over 5 s, screen unlocked); the window's place on screen checked once a second
result: the rise belongs to a window out of sight, not to Home. On 2026-10-31/11-01 the built-in display (120 Hz) ran a full-screen app; a walk window that opened there sat in a Space nobody saw and still drew. All 11 such runs rose pass over pass, any build (8 listed below; the other 3, a harness check and a profiled walk, reached 106.5 ms/s in pass 1, 304.4 in pass 3 and 676 ms/s of CPU) (trunk 96.2, 230.0, 322.7 ms/s; candidates 64.8 to 106.5 in pass 1, 182.2 to 412.3 in pass 2, 304.4 to 536.5 in pass 3; main-thread CPU up to 676 ms/s), and the page held more AppKit views each pass (63, 91, 105; shelf scroll views 5, 7, 8). Every run with the window on screen (external display, 60 Hz) stayed flat, with 77 views and 6 shelf scroll views after each pass in all of B9-3's runs. The walk now moves its window, never in front and without focus, to a display where it shows, and a run whose window left the screen is not counted

check: baseline: Home's scroll on trunk, window on screen, pointer elsewhere
how: the B9-1 walk of trunk 24a953268, 5 runs of 3 passes from 22:32 to 22:47, window on the external display (60 Hz, 16.67 ms frames), art cached on disk; gate at each start: load1 2.96 to 3.95, CPU idle 75.7 to 83.5 percent
result: hitch 28.1 to 47.7 ms/s (median of 15 passes 38.6), frame p50 and p95 16.67 ms in all 15 passes, p99 34.6 to 42.3 ms (one frame missed now and then), main-thread CPU 298 to 338 ms/s, no rise from pass to pass

check: three per-card candidates against trunk, interleaved
how: the B9-2 walk, 5 rounds of trunk and three candidates in turned order (trunk below counts B9-2's 5 runs and 5 more here), 22:50 to 00:37; only runs with the window on screen for the whole walk count (load1 2.57 to 3.98, idle 75.7 to 87.2 at each start). A = perf(apple): Home's cards carry no empty menu, one animation, no brightness layer; B = one pointer tracker per Home shelf instead of onHover on each card (b6a9e4c7b's idea on the current Shelf); D = A and B
result: no candidate moved the numbers beyond trunk's run-to-run spread; all three dropped. Run means of hitch (ms/s): trunk 30.7, 32.9, 34.8, 37.3, 41.0, 43.3, 44.7, 50.0 and two runs at 159.5 and 232.5; A 34.2, 35.2; B 26.0, 30.3, 34.4, 46.5; D 23.5, 36.2, 47.0, 55.9, 59.5. Main-thread CPU median: trunk 329.5, A 326.5, B 329, D 314 ms/s. The two high trunk runs match B9-4 (the Mac's pointer over the window)

check: what costs when the pointer rests over Home, as during a trackpad scroll
how: two trunk walks a few minutes apart, same build and gate (load1 3.45 and 3.14, idle 77.3 and 83.3), window on screen at 60 Hz; the walk records whether the Mac's pointer rested over the window (it never moves it). Time Profiler attached to two walks, main-thread samples over the three passes
result: pointer over the window: hitch 243.5, 236.6, 237.0 ms/s, frame p95 38.5 to 48.0 ms, CPU 337 to 360 ms/s; pointer elsewhere: 31.7, 27.5, 27.3 ms/s, p95 16.67 ms, CPU 295 to 331 ms/s. In a profiled walk with the pointer over the window (a candidate build, B9-5's E+F) SwiftUI sent hover to the cards on every scroll step (NSHostingView.didRequestHoverUpdate and EventBindingManager.send: 1,065 ms of main thread over 33 s); the profiled trunk walk with the pointer elsewhere had none. In the trunk profile: the navigation title preference reduced across every lazy row and card (NavigationTitleKey.reduce, 1,143 of 7,722 samples), the stack sizing the rows above the screen (LazyHVStack.lengthAndSpacing, 1,611) and new card views (makeElements, 919). The walk cannot rest a pointer on Home without moving the owner's, so hover candidates were measured only by B9-3's pointer-free runs

check: two layout candidates from the B9-4 profile
how: E = each Home row one view (RowView and the card that may follow it in one VStack, so the lazy stack does not rebuild a list per row); F = a navigation title written on Home's page on the Mac (the toolbar shows none), meant to stop the title preference at the page; EF = both. One Time Profiler walk of EF; then trunk, E and EF interleaved with the B9-1 gate, from 02:17
result: not shown, both dropped. The EF profile had fewer samples in the targeted work than the trunk profile (NavigationTitleKey.reduce 786 against 1,143, LazyHVStack.lengthAndSpacing 1,236 against 1,611, ForEach walking 1,327 against 1,744), so F does not stop the preference, and that walk also had the pointer over the window, so its totals do not compare. Interleaved runs with the window on screen and the pointer outside it: E passes 37.3, 35.1, 28.1 ms/s (mean 33.5), CPU 293 to 326; EF 44.5, 28.1, 35.7 (mean 36.1), CPU 294 to 327; trunk 86.5, 2.3, 12.8 (mean 33.9), CPU 280 to 340: one run each, at the level of B9-2's run means (32.9 to 44.7), and a trunk run whose passes spread from 2.3 to 86.5. The runs stopped at 02:55, when the external display went away and only the built-in display, running a full-screen app, was left: no window of the walk could show
